question.text: In a nuclear fission process, a high mass nuclide <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>236</mn><mo>)</mo></math> with binding energy <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>7</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi>MeV</mi><mo>/</mo></math>Nucleon dissociated into two middle mass nuclides <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>118</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, having binding energy of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi>MeV</mi><mo>/</mo></math>Nucleon. The energy released in the process would be _______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>MeV</mi></math>.

solution.text:
The formula to calculate the energy released in the given process can be written as

Q=BEProduct -BEReactant    ...1

From equation (1), it follows that

Q=2(118)(8.6)-236(7.6) MeV=236 MeV
